items.title: 8.1 Introduction to Online Research and Digital Literacy

source_refs.note: Topic 8.1 with the chapter introduction (PDF 195, printed 192). The learning outcomes (PDF 194) are not reproduced. Short question 1 is answered.

blocks.text: This chapter covers online research and digital literacy: conducting research online with advanced search techniques, managing digital resources, forming clear research questions, research ethics and intellectual property rights, so that students can do rigorous, ethical research and use digital content properly.

blocks.title: Online research
blocks.text: Online research is finding information about a topic on the internet from sources such as articles, reports and videos, aiming to collect correct, trustworthy and current information that helps understand a topic or solve a problem.

Check that information comes from reliable sources, such as official government websites, educational institutions or well-known newspapers, and compare several sources to make sure the findings are accurate.

blocks.prompt: How can you make sure information found online is reliable (short question 1)?
blocks.explanation: Use reliable sources such as official, educational or well-known news sites; check who wrote it and when; and compare it with several other sources before trusting it.

items: Online research: find correct, trustworthy, current information; check sources and compare them.
